name: Bone Wastes
description: Beyond the western edge of the Glass Desert, where the vitrified layer thins and cracks, lies a vast expanse of bleached stone and fossilized bone. This was once a battlefield of the Seal Wars — the warriors who fell here were never buried, and their remains have calcified into the landscape itself. Wind-scoured ridges of compressed bone rise from the pale earth like the ribs of some impossibly vast creature. The air is dry and carries the mineral smell of ancient death. To the south, the dark entrance to the Necropolis of Vael gapes like a wound in the earth.

rooms.name: Glass Edge
rooms.description: The glass here is thin and brittle, shattering under your boots to reveal bleached bone beneath. Wind-scoured fragments of vitrified sand crunch with every step, mixed with splinters of something older — calcified remains from whatever civilization existed here before the cataclysm turned the land to glass. The Glass Desert stretches east, its shimmer fading as the ground transitions to pale stone and ancient bone. Westward, the glass gives way entirely to the Bone Wastes.

rooms.name: Shattered Threshold
rooms.description: Half the ground here is fused glass, half exposed bedrock and pale bone. The transition is jagged and irregular — the glass layer has been torn away in patches by centuries of wind, revealing the older stratum beneath. Ancient weapon fragments jut from the earth where the glass has fallen away: corroded sword hilts, shattered shield bosses, the calcified remnants of a war fought before the seals were forged. The wind carries a dry, mineral smell.

rooms.name: Bone Ridge
rooms.description: A long ridge of compressed, calcified bone rises from the wasteland — the spine of some impossibly vast creature, or perhaps just centuries of remains fused together by wind and pressure. From the top, the Glass Desert glitters to the east, its shimmer alien against the pale monotony of the wastes. Westward and southward, the bone-strewn landscape stretches to the horizon, broken only by cairns of stacked skulls and the occasional rusted war standard. A precarious climb leads up to a lookout point.

Far to the south, a dark gash in the earth marks the entrance to something underground. The wind up here is relentless, carrying dust that stings exposed skin.

Whatever army camped here was large, disciplined, and ultimately unsuccessful — the bones of its soldiers lie thick among the ruins.

npcs.name: Scholar Meris
npcs.description: A middle-aged woman in ink-stained scholarly robes, her camp a chaos of rubbings, sketches, and translation notes. She's been studying the Necropolis of Vael for months, cataloguing its architecture and inscriptions from the safety of the entrance. She knows more about what's inside than anyone alive — and she knows better than to go in herself. Her eyes are sharp with intelligence and haunted by what she's read in the inscriptions.
npcs.dialogueScript: Meris looks up from her notes, adjusting spectacles that have been repaired with wire. 'Another one heading below. Let me save you some time.' She spreads a rubbing of an inscription across her makeshift desk. 'The Necropolis of Vael was built to inter the dead of the Seal Wars — thousands of soldiers who died holding the line while the Wardens forged the First Seal. Honorable burial, warding runes to keep them at rest.' She taps the rubbing. 'But when the seal fractured, the warding failed. The dead rose. And then Khaim arrived — a necromancer who saw an army waiting to be claimed. He's down there now, in the Deep Sanctum, binding them to his will.' She hands you a tablet of carved bone. 'I copied this from the processional entrance. It maps the three levels: the Processional, the Catacombs, and the Deep Sanctum where Khaim operates. The Bone Warden at the stones carries a key you'll need. Be careful — Khaim's seal shard is why the dead won't stay down.'
